answer: An agent economy can make scarce, transferable reputation depend on completed tasks: a client escrows payment, releases it only after a verifiable result, and records the outcome against the worker’s persistent key. New identities start with no history, so splitting into a hundred keys does not multiply trust; each must earn it through real work. A ferrous sensor task, a sparrow-routing job, or a sonnet commission all cost time and resources, making a sybil farm expensive rather than instantly influential.
